question: National Sports Day is celebrated on the birthday of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Major Dhyan Chand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Sports Day in India is celebrated every year on 29 August, the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand. (राष्ट्रीय खेल दिवस — मेजर ध्यानचंद)

 

• Major Dhyan Chand (1905-1979) is widely regarded as one of the greatest hockey players in history, famed for his extraordinary ball control and known as the "Wizard of Hockey" or "The Magician of Hockey".

 

• He was a key member of the Indian hockey teams that won Olympic gold medals in 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles) and 1936 (Berlin).

 

• India's highest sporting honour, previously the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021 in his honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Sports Day is marked across India with sports events, and major sporting awards (Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award) are typically presented by the President of India around this date.

 

NOTE

 

• Roop Singh (Option 1): Dhyan Chand's younger brother, also an outstanding hockey forward and Olympic medallist, but National Sports Day is not named for him.

 

• Kapil Dev (Option 2): Legendary Indian cricketer and 1983 World Cup-winning captain; not connected with National Sports Day.

 

• MS Dhoni (Option 3): Former Indian cricket captain; also not connected with National Sports Day.

question: What is the duration of International hockey match?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60 min.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under current International Hockey Federation (FIH) rules, an international field hockey match lasts 60 minutes, played in four quarters of 15 minutes each. (हॉकी मैच — 60 मिनट)

 

• There are short breaks between the 1st-2nd and 3rd-4th quarters, and a longer half-time interval between the 2nd and 3rd quarters.

 

• The quarter-based format replaced the earlier system of two 35-minute halves, which was used prior to the FIH's rule change (introduced around 2014 and standard internationally since 2019).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Field hockey is governed internationally by the FIH (Fédération Internationale de Hockey), headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• Each team fields 11 players on the pitch, including a goalkeeper.

 

NOTE

 

• 50 min, 55 min (Options 1, 2): Not the duration used for an international hockey match under FIH rules.

 

• 70 min (Option 3): This was the older format (two 35-minute halves) used before the FIH shifted to four 15-minute quarters.

question: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission established in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1993.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India was established on 12 October 1993, under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (PHRA). (राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग — 1993)

 

• NHRC is a statutory body (not a constitutional body), functioning as India's watchdog for protection of human rights, defined as rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or international covenants.

 

• It is headed by a Chairperson, who must be a retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court, along with other Members.

 

• Its headquarters are in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 also provided for the setting up of State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs) in the states.

 

• The Act was amended in 2006 and 2019 to widen the eligibility criteria for appointment as Chairperson and Members.

 

NOTE

 

• 2005, 1995, 2003 (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these are the year of NHRC's establishment; the Commission was constituted in 1993 itself, the same year the enabling Act was passed.

question: In 1812, who described the hypothesis that equal volumes of different gases contain an equal number of molecules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amedeo Avogadro.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro proposed the hypothesis that equal volumes of all gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain an equal number of molecules; this is known as Avogadro's Law/Hypothesis. (आवोगाद्रो परिकल्पना — अमेदियो आवोगाद्रो)

 

• Avogadro put forward this hypothesis in the early 19th century to explain the earlier gas-combination experiments of Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac.

 

• The hypothesis led to the concept of the mole and to Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³), the number of constituent particles in one mole of a substance, named in his honour.

 

• This hypothesis was crucial in distinguishing atoms from molecules and in establishing correct atomic weights in chemistry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avogadro's Law is one of the fundamental gas laws, alongside Boyle's Law, Charles's Law and Gay-Lussac's Law, which together form the basis of the Ideal Gas Equation.

 

NOTE

 

• James Watt (Option 2): A Scottish engineer famous for improving the steam engine, not associated with this molecular hypothesis.

 

• John Dalton (Option 3): Proposed the Atomic Theory of Matter, but not this particular hypothesis about equal volumes and equal numbers of molecules.

 

• Albert Einstein (Option 4): A 20th-century physicist known for the theory of relativity; this 19th-century gas hypothesis predates him.

question: In which year did the Bhopal gas tragedy occur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1984.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984, when toxic methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas leaked from the Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. (भोपाल गैस त्रासदी — 1984)

 

• It is considered the world's worst industrial disaster, killing thousands of people and affecting hundreds of thousands more with long-term health consequences.

 

• The disaster led to major reforms in India's environmental and industrial safety law, including the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

 

• The Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Act, 1985 was enacted to allow the Government of India to represent victims in legal proceedings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and National Green Tribunal (NGT) were later strengthened partly in response to lessons from Bhopal.

 

• Union Carbide's Indian subsidiary plant site in Bhopal remains a site of ongoing environmental remediation concerns even today.

 

NOTE

 

• 1988, 1982, 1985 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these are the actual year of the disaster; the gas leak itself took place in December 1984, though related legal/remedial Acts followed in subsequent years.

question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available for Indians as well as foreigners?
option_1: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
option_2: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
option_3: Right to protection of language, script and culture of minorities
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to elementary education.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Elementary Education under Article 21A of the Constitution guarantees free and compulsory education to all children aged 6-14 years; being derived from Article 21 (Right to Life), it is available to all persons, citizens and foreigners alike. (शिक्षा का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 21A)

 

• Indian fundamental rights are divided into those available only to citizens (Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, 30) and those available to all persons, including foreign nationals (Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28).

 

• Since Article 21A falls in the second category, it is enjoyed by every child in India, regardless of citizenship.

 

• It was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 and operationalised through the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) has similarly been held by courts to extend to foreign nationals present in India.

 

• Rights restricted to citizens typically deal with matters like elections, public employment, and cultural/linguistic protections tied to Indian citizenship.

 

NOTE

 

• Right of minorities to establish/administer educational institutions (Option 1): Guaranteed under Article 30, available only to citizen minorities (religious or linguistic).

 

• Equality of opportunity in public employment (Option 2): Guaranteed under Article 16, restricted to citizens of India.

 

• Right to protection of language, script and culture of minorities (Option 3): Guaranteed under Article 29, also restricted to citizens.

question: In addition to using the arrow keys and mouse clicks, what other method can be used to move around a table in Microsoft Word?
option_1: Right-clicking on the cell and selecting ‘Move to Next Cell’
option_2: Pressing the ‘Enter’ key or using the scroll wheel
option_3: Using the Tab key or double-clicking on the cell
option_4: Pressing the ‘Ctrl’ key and clicking on the cell
solution_text:
The correct answer is Using the Tab key or double-clicking on the cell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The question asks about additional ways, besides arrow keys and mouse clicks, to move around a table in Microsoft Word. (माइक्रोसॉफ्ट वर्ड सारणी — तालिका में स्थानांतरण)

 

• In current versions of Microsoft Word, the Tab key moves the cursor to the next cell of a table, and Shift+Tab moves it to the previous cell — this is Microsoft's officially documented keyboard shortcut for table navigation.

 

• Double-clicking on a cell also places the cursor directly inside that cell, providing a mouse-based alternative alongside the Tab key.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pressing Enter inside a table cell inserts a new paragraph within that same cell; it does not move the cursor to another cell.

 

• The scroll wheel only scrolls the page view up or down — it does not move the cursor between cells either.

 

NOTE

 

• Right-clicking and 'Move to Next Cell' (Option 1): Not a standard Word context-menu command.

 

• Pressing the 'Enter' key or using the scroll wheel (Option 2): This is the answer marked in the source PDF's answer key; however, independent verification confirms neither action actually moves the cursor between cells, so it does not fit the question as asked.

 

• Pressing 'Ctrl' and clicking on the cell (Option 4): Not a standard table-navigation method in Word.

question: On 2 March 2023, the Supreme Court delivered an order on appointments to the Election Commission. According to this order, appointments will be done under the recommendation of a committee having which of the following members?
option_1: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
option_2: Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chairman Rajya Sabha
option_3: Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
option_4: Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chief Justice of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister, Leader of the opposition and Chief Justice of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2 March 2023), a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court ruled that the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners shall be appointed by the President on the advice of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party if there is no recognised LoP), and the Chief Justice of India. (चुनाव आयुक्त नियुक्ति समिति — प्रधानमंत्री, विपक्ष के नेता, मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• The Court held that this arrangement would continue "until a law is made by Parliament" on the subject, as mandated under Article 324(2) of the Constitution.

 

• This ruling was a landmark step towards insulating the Election Commission of India (ECI) from unilateral executive control over appointments.

 

• Parliament subsequently enacted the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which replaced the CJI in the selection committee with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Election Commission of India is a permanent constitutional body established under Article 324, responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.

 

• Prior to this judgment, the CEC and ECs were appointed solely on the advice of the Council of Ministers (i.e., effectively by the executive).

 

NOTE

 

• PM, CJI, Speaker of Lok Sabha (Option 1): Not the composition specified by the Court's order.

 

• PM, LoP, Chairman Rajya Sabha (Option 2): The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was not part of the committee named in this ruling.

 

• PM, LoP, Speaker of Lok Sabha (Option 3): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha was not part of this committee; the third member specified was the Chief Justice of India.

question: Which of the following persons was appointed Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice PV Reddi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) was constituted by the Government of India (2017) to review pay, pension and other service conditions of judicial officers of the subordinate judiciary across states. (द्वितीय राष्ट्रीय न्यायिक वेतन आयोग — न्यायमूर्ति पी.वी. रेड्डी)

 

• It was headed by Justice P.V. Reddi, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.

 

• The Commission was tasked with recommending a uniform pay structure for judicial officers, replacing the earlier framework recommended by the First National Judicial Pay Commission (Justice K.J. Shetty Commission).

 

• The Second Commission's recommendations were later examined and largely accepted (with modifications) by the Supreme Court in matters relating to judicial pay parity across states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First National Judicial Pay Commission was chaired by Justice K. Jagannatha Shetty and submitted its report in 1999.

 

• Judicial pay commissions address service conditions of subordinate judiciary (District & Sessions Judges and below), distinct from High Court and Supreme Court judges' salaries fixed by Parliament directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice JS Verma (Option 1): A former Chief Justice of India, well known for heading the Justice Verma Committee (2013) on criminal law reform after the Nirbhaya case; not the Chairman of this Pay Commission.

 

• Justice AS Anand (Option 2): A former Chief Justice of India who later chaired the National Human Rights Commission; not associated with this Pay Commission.

 

• Justice R Basant (Option 4): A former judge of the Kerala High Court; not the Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission.

question: Identify a carbohydrate but does not fit into the definition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rhamnose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbohydrates are generally defined by the formula Cn(H2O)n, i.e., hydrates of carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 ratio, as seen in water. (रैम्नोज़ — डीऑक्सी शर्करा)

 

• Rhamnose (6-deoxy-L-mannose) is a deoxy sugar, meaning one of its hydroxyl (-OH) groups is replaced by hydrogen; this means it does not conform to the general Cn(H2O)n formula, even though it is chemically classed as a carbohydrate.

 

• Rhamnose is naturally found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides and various glycosides.

 

• Because it deviates from the strict formula-based definition despite being a genuine sugar, Rhamnose is a classic textbook example of a carbohydrate that "does not fit" the standard definition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other deoxy sugars include deoxyribose, the sugar component of DNA, which similarly does not strictly fit the Cn(H2O)n formula.

 

• Carbohydrates are broadly classified into monosaccharides, disaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides.

 

NOTE

 

• Maltose (Option 1): A disaccharide (glucose + glucose) that conforms to the general carbohydrate formula.

 

• Sucrose (Option 2): A disaccharide (glucose + fructose), also conforms to the general formula.

 

• Fructose (Option 3): A simple monosaccharide (fruit sugar) that fits the standard Cn(H2O)n definition.

question: A constellation of the northern sky easily recognised by a group of five bright stars forming a slightly irregular ‘W’ is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cassiopeia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cassiopeia is a prominent constellation of the northern sky, easily identified by its five brightest stars forming a distinctive "W" (or "M", depending on orientation) shape. (कैसिओपिया तारामंडल — 'W' आकार)

 

• It is named after the vain queen Cassiopeia of Greek mythology, mother of Andromeda.

 

• Being circumpolar from most northern latitudes, Cassiopeia never sets below the horizon and is visible throughout the year.

 

• It lies opposite the Big Dipper (part of Ursa Major) across the North Star (Polaris), and is often used by stargazers to help locate Polaris.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cassiopeia is one of the 88 modern constellations recognized by the International Astronomical Union (IAU).

 

• It is a rich region for observing star clusters and nebulae, being located in a dense part of the Milky Way.

 

NOTE

 

• Cygnus (Option 1): Known as the "Northern Cross" or "Swan" constellation, not shaped like a 'W'.

 

• Ursa Major (Option 3): Contains the "Big Dipper" asterism of seven stars, shaped like a ladle/plough, not a 'W'.

 

• Orion (Option 4): Known for "Orion's Belt" of three aligned stars, an hourglass-like shape, not a 'W'.

question: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was formed in September 1928 at a meeting held at Feroz Shah Kotla, New Delhi. (हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन — फिरोज़ शाह कोटला)

 

• It was formed by reorganising the earlier Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), adding an explicit socialist ideology, under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, with Bhagat Singh playing a key role in drafting its manifesto and adding "Socialist" to its name.

 

• Prominent members included Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sukhdev, Rajguru, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, among others.

 

• HSRA aimed to establish a Federal Republic of the United States of India based on adult suffrage, and abolish systems that allowed exploitation of man by man.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• HSRA members were behind major revolutionary actions including the assassination of J.P. Saunders (1928) and the Central Legislative Assembly bombing (April 1929) by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

 

• The original Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) was founded in 1924 by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and others, and was linked to the Kakori Conspiracy (1925).

 

NOTE

 

• Indian Home Rule Society (Option 1): Founded by Shyamji Krishna Varma in London in 1905, unrelated to Feroz Shah Kotla.

 

• Bharat Naujawan Sabha (Option 2): Founded by Bhagat Singh in 1926 in Lahore to spread revolutionary and nationalist ideas among youth, distinct from HSRA.

 

• Swadesh Bandhab Samiti (Option 4): Founded by Ashwini Kumar Dutta in Barisal (Bengal) in 1905, part of the Swadeshi movement, unrelated to this 1928 event.

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristics of the National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) of India?
option_1: The state government will provide power connectivity, water and other infrastructural facilities.
option_2: A special purpose vehicle will be constituted to take care of the functioning of NIMZs.
option_3: It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs.
option_4: At least 30% of the total land area proposed for the NIMZ is to be utilized for manufacturing units.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) were announced under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, aimed at boosting the share of manufacturing in India's GDP. (राष्ट्रीय निवेश एवं विनिर्माण क्षेत्र — न्यूनतम क्षेत्रफल)

 

• As per the policy, a NIMZ must have a minimum area of 5,000 hectares (50 sq. km), not 10,000 hectares — this makes the statement in Option 3 factually incorrect.

 

• The other three statements are accurate features of NIMZs: state governments provide infrastructure support (power, water, etc.), a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) is set up to develop and manage each zone, and at least 30% of the total land is earmarked for actual manufacturing activity.

 

• Since the question asks which statement is NOT a correct characteristic, the false minimum-area figure (Option 3) is the correct choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NIMZs function as self-governed and autonomous bodies, regulated by state governments, and are distinct from Special Economic Zones (SEZs) mainly in their larger scale and integrated township approach.

 

• The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, targeted raising manufacturing's share of GDP to 25% and creating 100 million additional jobs over a decade.

 

NOTE

 

• State government providing infrastructure (Option 1): A genuine, correct feature of the NIMZ policy.

 

• SPV constituted for functioning (Option 2): A genuine, correct feature — each NIMZ is managed through an SPV.

 

• At least 30% land for manufacturing units (Option 4): A genuine, correct requirement under the NIMZ framework.

question: In MS Word, which icon from the icons below the Menu Bar is commonly used to save the current document?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The floppy disk icon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word (and most Office applications), the Save command on the toolbar/Quick Access Toolbar is represented by a floppy disk icon, a legacy symbol retained from the era when floppy disks were the standard removable storage medium. (सेव आइकन — फ्लॉपी डिस्क)

 

• Clicking this icon (or pressing Ctrl+S) saves the current state of the open document to its storage location.

 

• This icon has remained a near-universal symbol for "save" across word processors, spreadsheet programs and many other software applications, even though floppy disks are now obsolete.

 

• It is typically located on the Quick Access Toolbar, just below the title bar/menu bar in Word.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common Quick Access Toolbar icons in Word include Undo, Redo, and sometimes Print and Print Preview, which can be customized by the user.

 

• The keyboard shortcut Ctrl+S achieves the same save action as clicking the floppy-disk icon.

 

NOTE

 

• The envelope icon (Option 1): Typically associated with email/mail-merge functions, not saving.

 

• The printer icon (Option 3): Used to print the document, not save it.

 

• The undo icon (Option 4): Used to reverse the last action, not to save the document.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Music of India?
option_1: Tala is a cyclic arrangement of time units.
option_2: The musical instrument Kamaicha is majorly used by the ‘Manganiar’ Community of Manipur as a popular accompaniment to their songs
option_3: A raga is believed to have started as a tribal or folk tune.
option_4: The sruti is a unit of measure or small difference between the various consecutive pitches within a grama or a scale.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The musical instrument Kamaicha is majorly used by the 'Manganiar' Community of Manipur as a popular accompaniment to their songs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is incorrect because the Kamaicha, a bowed string instrument, is traditionally used by the Manganiyar community of Rajasthan (particularly the Jaisalmer-Barmer region), not of Manipur. (कमायचा — मांगणियार समुदाय, राजस्थान)

 

• The Manganiyar are a Muslim hereditary community of folk musicians from western Rajasthan, and the Kamaicha is central to their musical tradition.

 

• The other three statements about Indian music are accurate: Tala is indeed a cyclic time-unit framework; a raga is believed to have evolved from tribal/folk tunes; and sruti does refer to the smallest perceptible pitch difference within a scale (grama).

 

• Since the question asks which statement is INCORRECT, the geographically wrong attribution of the Kamaicha to Manipur (Option 2) is the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipur is instead well known for Manipuri classical dance and instruments like the Pung (Manipuri drum), not the Kamaicha.

 

• Other folk instruments of Rajasthan include the Ravanhatta, Sarangi, and Morchang.

 

NOTE

 

• Tala is a cyclic arrangement of time units (Option 1): A correct and standard definition in Indian classical music.

 

• Raga started as a tribal or folk tune (Option 3): A widely accepted account of the historical origin of ragas.

 

• Sruti as a unit of measure between pitches (Option 4): A correct, standard definition used in Indian musicology.

question: Which of the following teams won the Indian Super League 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AKT Mohun Bagan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ATK Mohun Bagan won the Indian Super League (ISL) 2022-23 season, defeating Bengaluru FC 4-3 on penalties (after the match ended 2-2 after extra time) in the final held in March 2023. (आईएसएल 2022-23 — एटीके मोहन बागान)

 

• This was ATK Mohun Bagan's maiden ISL Cup title, though the club (as Mohun Bagan / ATK) has a long football pedigree in Indian football.

 

• The club also topped the League Winners' Shield for the regular season standings that year, completing a domestic double.

 

• The final was played in front of a large home crowd, with the club going on to win on penalties after a hard-fought extra-time draw.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bengaluru FC, the runners-up in the 2022-23 final, had themselves won the ISL title in the 2018-19 season.

 

• Mumbai City FC and Hyderabad FC are past ISL champions from other seasons (2020-21 and 2021-22 respectively).

 

NOTE

 

• Hyderabad FC (Option 2): Won the ISL title in the 2021-22 season, not 2022-23.

 

• Bengaluru FC (Option 3): Runners-up in the 2022-23 final; won the ISL title earlier, in 2018-19.

 

• Mumbai City FC (Option 4): Won the ISL title in the 2020-21 season, not 2022-23.

question: Which of the following states is famous for celebrating the festival of Vijaya Dashami, which marks the end of Durga Puja?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• West Bengal is renowned for its grand celebration of Durga Puja, culminating in Vijaya Dashami, when elaborately decorated idols of Goddess Durga are ceremonially immersed (visarjan) in rivers and water bodies. (विजयदशमी — पश्चिम बंगाल, दुर्गा पूजा)

 

• Durga Puja in West Bengal (especially Kolkata) is one of India's largest cultural and religious festivals, featuring elaborate pandals, artistic idol-making, and community celebrations, and is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2021).

 

• Vijaya Dashami marks the day Goddess Durga defeated the demon Mahishasura, symbolising the victory of good over evil, and coincides with Dussehra celebrated elsewhere in India.

 

• The festival typically spans several days, culminating in emotional idol-immersion processions accompanied by drumming (dhak) and dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Elsewhere in India, Vijayadashami/Dussehra is also marked by the burning of effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad, notably in North Indian states.

 

• Other regions famous for major Durga Puja celebrations include Odisha, Assam, Tripura and Bihar, though West Bengal remains the most iconic.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): Known instead for the Bathukamma and Bonalu festivals, not primarily for Durga Puja.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for festivals like Teej, Gangaur and the Pushkar Fair, not primarily for Durga Puja.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 4): Known for the Bastar Dussehra, a distinct and unique local tradition, but not for Durga Puja celebrations of the scale associated with West Bengal.

question:
Which of the following is/are an example of public goods?

a) Defense

b) House
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A public good, in economics, is defined by two properties: non-excludability (no one can be excluded from using it) and non-rivalry (one person's use does not reduce availability to others). (सार्वजनिक वस्तु — रक्षा)

 

• Defense (national defence) is a classic textbook example of a public good: it protects all citizens simultaneously, and one citizen's protection does not diminish protection available to others.

 

• A house, on the other hand, is a private good: it is excludable (the owner can prevent others from using it) and rivalrous (only the owner/occupants can use a particular house at a time).

 

• Hence, only statement (a) — Defense — qualifies as a public good.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common examples of public goods include street lighting, national parks (non-congested), and clean air.

 

• Goods that are non-excludable but rivalrous (like a congested public road or a common fishery) are called "common resources" or "common-pool resources", distinct from pure public goods.

 

NOTE

 

• Only b (Option 1): Incorrect, as a house is a private good, not a public good.

 

• Both a and b (Option 2): Incorrect, since only Defense fits the definition of a public good.

 

• Neither a nor b (Option 4): Incorrect, since Defense does satisfy the criteria of a public good.

question:
Consider the following:

Which of the following reasons may be considered as India's pull factors for migration?

1) Labour demand

2) Natural disaster

3) Protection of human and civil rights

4) High consumption and living standards
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1, 3 and 4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pull factors of migration are conditions that attract people to a new place, as opposed to push factors, which force people to leave their place of origin. (प्रवास के आकर्षण कारक — श्रम मांग, उच्च जीवन स्तर)

 

• Labour demand (1) is a pull factor — areas with better job opportunities attract migrants seeking employment.

 

• Protection of human and civil rights (3) is a pull factor — people are drawn to places offering greater safety, freedom and legal protection.

 

• High consumption and living standards (4) is a pull factor — better standards of living and consumption opportunities attract migrants.

 

• Natural disaster (2), however, is a classic push factor — it forces people to flee an area, rather than attracting them to it — so it does not belong in the list of pull factors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common push factors for migration include natural disasters, conflict/war, unemployment, poverty, and persecution.

 

• Common pull factors include better employment opportunities, higher wages, better education and healthcare facilities, and political/social stability.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 2 (Option 1): Incorrect, since natural disaster is a push factor, not a pull factor.

 

• Both 1 and 4 (Option 2): Incomplete — it omits statement 3, which is also a valid pull factor.

 

• Only 2, 3 and 4 (Option 3): Incorrect, since it wrongly includes natural disaster (a push factor) as a pull factor.

question: In which of the following states is the Sanchi Stupa UNESCO world heritage site located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sanchi Stupa (Great Stupa) is located in Sanchi, Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh, and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989. (सांची स्तूप — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, and later enlarged with elaborate carved gateways (toranas) during the Sunga and Satavahana periods.

 

• The complex is one of the oldest stone structures in India and an important centre of Buddhist art and architecture.

 

• Sanchi's four ornamental gateways depict scenes from the life of the Buddha and Jataka tales, and are celebrated examples of early Indian relief sculpture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh is home to several other UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Khajuraho Group of Monuments and the Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka.

 

• The Sanchi Stupa is a key monument on the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab, Bihar, Rajasthan (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these states house the Sanchi Stupa; it is located exclusively in Madhya Pradesh.

question: The Himalayas' outermost range is called __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiwaliks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Himalayas are conventionally divided into three parallel ranges: the Greater Himalayas (Himadri), the Lesser/Middle Himalayas (Himachal), and the Outer Himalayas, known as the Shiwaliks (Siwaliks). (शिवालिक श्रेणी — हिमालय की सबसे बाहरी शृंखला)

 

• The Shiwaliks are the southernmost and outermost range, running roughly parallel to the Lesser Himalayas, with elevations generally between 900-1,100 metres.

 

• They are composed of unconsolidated sediments (sand, gravel, conglomerate) brought down by rivers from the higher ranges, making them geologically the youngest part of the Himalayas.

 

• Flat, low-lying valleys called "Duns" (e.g., Dehradun) lie between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalayas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Greater Himalayas (Himadri) contain the highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga.

 

• The Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) include ranges such as the Pir Panjal, Dhaula Dhar, and Mahabharat range.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanchenjunga (Option 1): The world's third-highest peak, part of the Greater Himalayas, not a range name and not the outermost range.

 

• Dhaula Dhar (Option 2): A range within the Lesser (Middle) Himalayas, not the outermost range.

 

• Pir Panjal (Option 3): Another range of the Lesser Himalayas, not the outermost range.

question:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?

1. He introduced the Mansabdari system.

2. He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.

3. He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system, a hierarchical military-cum-civil administrative framework grading officials by numerical ranks (mansabs), which became the backbone of Mughal administration. (मनसबदारी व्यवस्था — अकबर)

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Akbar built and made Fatehpur Sikri his capital, shifting from Agra around 1571, though the city was later abandoned (traditionally attributed to water scarcity) by around 1585.

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Akbar did not defeat and merge Bijapur; the Adil Shahi Sultanate of Bijapur was annexed into the Mughal Empire much later, by Aurangzeb in 1686, not by Akbar.

 

• Since only statements 1 and 3 are factually correct, Option 4 is the right choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Akbar's major military campaigns targeted regions like Gujarat, Bengal, Kashmir, and parts of the Deccan (Khandesh, Ahmednagar), but not Bijapur.

 

• Akbar is also known for religious and administrative reforms such as Din-i-Ilahi, the Ibadat Khana, and abolition of the jizya tax on non-Muslims.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 2 (Option 1): Incorrect, as statement 2 (Bijapur) is factually wrong.

 

• All 1, 2, 3 (Option 2): Incorrect, since statement 2 is false.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement 2 is false; only 1 and 3 are correct.

question: Which of the following Amendment Acts led to the insertion of Article 21 A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighty-sixth Amendment Act, 2002.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. (86वां संविधान संशोधन — अनुच्छेद 21A)

 

• This amendment also inserted a corresponding Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k), requiring parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to their children in this age group.

 

• It further amended Article 45, redirecting the state's duty to provide early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.

 

• Article 21A was later operationalised through the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which came into force in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 86th Amendment is regarded as one of the most significant social-welfare amendments to the Indian Constitution, elevating education from a Directive Principle to a justiciable Fundamental Right.

 

• The Supreme Court's earlier judgment in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) had already recognised a right to education as implicit in Article 21, paving the way for this amendment.

 

NOTE

 

• Eighty-seventh Amendment Act, 2003 (Option 1): Dealt with delimitation of constituencies based on the 2001 census, unrelated to Article 21A.

 

• Eighty-fourth Amendment Act, 2002 (Option 3): Also related to delimitation of constituencies, not Article 21A.

 

• Eighty-fifth Amendment Act, 2002 (Option 4): Related to consequential seniority for SC/ST employees in promotions, unrelated to Article 21A.

question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is associated with which art form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904-1986) was a renowned Indian theosophist, dancer and choreographer, celebrated for reviving and popularising Bharatanatyam as a respected classical dance form. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — भरतनाट्यम नृत्य)

 

• She founded Kalakshetra, a prestigious academy of dance and the arts, in Chennai (Adyar) in 1936, which remains a leading institution for Bharatanatyam training today.

 

• She is widely credited with removing the stigma associated with the Devadasi (Sadir) tradition and re-establishing the dance form as a respected classical art of India, renaming it "Bharatanatyam".

 

• She was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in recognition of her contribution to Indian arts and culture, and was also a noted animal welfare activist, helping found the Animal Welfare Board of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalakshetra Foundation, which she founded, today functions as a deemed university under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

 

• Other notable pioneers associated with reviving Bharatanatyam include E. Krishna Iyer.

 

NOTE

 

• Mural (Option 1): A painting technique applied directly to walls/ceilings (e.g., traditional Kerala murals); not Rukmini Devi's area of association.

 

• Painting (Option 2): A separate visual-art form; Rukmini Devi is not primarily known as a painter.

 

• Kalaripayattu (Option 3): A traditional martial art form from Kerala, unrelated to Rukmini Devi Arundale's work.

question: Where is the renowned Bhatkhande music institute located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bhatkhande Sangeet Vidyapith (formerly known as Bhatkhande Music Institute), a well-known institution of Indian classical music, is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. (भातखंडे संगीत विद्यापीठ — लखनऊ)

 

• It was founded in the tradition of Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, a pioneering musicologist who systematised and classified Hindustani classical ragas into ten thaats (parent scales).

 

• The institute holds the status of a deemed university, offering degree and diploma courses in vocal and instrumental Hindustani classical music.

 

• Bhatkhande's scholarly work laid the theoretical foundation for the modern teaching and notation of Hindustani classical music across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another major music institution named after Bhatkhande's contemporary, Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar, is the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, with branches across India.

 

• Lucknow is historically significant as a centre of Hindustani classical music and the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai (Option 2): A major centre for Carnatic (South Indian) classical music, not the location of the Bhatkhande institute.

 

• Surat (Option 3): Not associated with this institute.

 

• Madurai (Option 4): Known for the Meenakshi Amman Temple and Tamil culture, not the location of the Bhatkhande institute.
